title: Linked List Cycle (Detect)
statement:
Given head, the head of a linked list, determine if the linked list has a cycle in it.

There is a cycle in a linked list if there is some node in the list that can be reached again by continuously following the next pointer.

Input format represents the list elements and a `pos` integer representing the 0-indexed position where the tail connects to form a cycle. If `pos` is -1, there is no cycle.
Note: your code will receive `pos`, so you can just simulate the cycle detection (Floyd's Tortoise and Hare algorithm) by building the list with the cycle, and then returning `YES` if a cycle is detected, or `NO` otherwise. Do not just check if `pos != -1`.
inputFormat:
Line 1: two integers N and pos.
Line 2: N space-separated integers representing the node values.
constraints:
0 <= N <= 10^4
-10^5 <= Node.val <= 10^5
pos is -1 or a valid index in the linked-list.
